This is the complete step-by-step sequence from the classroom presentation.

::: {.callout-important title="Safety and tools"}
Wear safety glasses when trimming conductors. Work only on an unplugged cable. Use the demonstrated stripper, cutter, and crimper. Keep wire clippings off the floor.
:::

:::: {.tej-visual-grid}
::: {.tej-visual-card}
![Cable stripper, cable tester, punch-down tool, and modular crimper.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:Redirect/file/Cable_stripper%2C_cable_tester_%28RJ45%2C_RJ11%29%2C_LSA-Tool_and_crimping_tool.jpg)

### Tools

Cable, matching 8P8C plugs, stripper/cutter, crimper, tester, ruler, and scrap container.

*Figure 1. Tools. [Open source and CC BY 4.0 licence.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cable_stripper,_cable_tester_(RJ45,_RJ11),_LSA-Tool_and_crimping_tool.jpg)*
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
![Eight conductors arranged in T568B order.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:Redirect/file/RJ-45_TIA-568B_Right.png)

### T568B order

Use the same order on both ends for this straight-through cable.

*Figure 2. [Open source and licence.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RJ-45_TIA-568B_Right.png)*
:::
::::

::: {.tej-wire-order}
<span>1 white-orange</span><span>2 orange</span><span>3 white-green</span><span>4 blue</span><span>5 white-blue</span><span>6 green</span><span>7 white-brown</span><span>8 brown</span>
:::

## Procedure

::: {.tej-step-grid}
::: {.tej-step-card}
<span class="tej-step-number">0</span>

### Measure and cut

Leave enough cable for a gentle route and a small service loop.
:::

::: {.tej-step-card}
<span class="tej-step-number">1</span>

### Remove the outer jacket

Strip about 25 to 40 mm. Cut lightly. Do not nick the eight insulated conductors.
:::

::: {.tej-step-card}
<span class="tej-step-number">2</span>

### Inspect every conductor

If copper is exposed or insulation is cut, remove the damaged section and start again.
:::

::: {.tej-step-card}
<span class="tej-step-number">3</span>

### Untangle and flatten

Separate the four pairs. Untwist only the length needed to reach the plug.
:::

::: {.tej-step-card}
<span class="tej-step-number">4</span>

### Arrange T568B

Place all eight conductors in the colour order shown above.
:::

::: {.tej-step-card}
<span class="tej-step-number">5</span>

### Trim to an even 13 mm

Pinch the order between your fingers. Cut the ends straight and even.
:::

::: {.tej-step-card}
<span class="tej-step-number">6</span>

### Insert and verify

Clip down, gold pins up, white-orange on the left. Every wire reaches the front. About 6 mm of jacket enters the plug.
:::

::: {.tej-step-card}
<span class="tej-step-number">7</span>

### Crimp

Insert the plug fully into the correct crimper slot. Squeeze completely using the demonstrated tool procedure.
:::

::: {.tej-step-card}
<span class="tej-step-number">8</span>

### Inspect the termination

All contacts sit evenly. The strain relief grips the jacket. Gently tug the cable.
:::

::: {.tej-step-card}
<span class="tej-step-number">9</span>

### Finish the other end and test

Use T568B again. A good tester shows pins 1 through 8 in the same order at both ends.
:::
:::

:::: {.tej-visual-grid}
::: {.tej-visual-card}
![Outer jacket being removed from an Ethernet cable.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:Redirect/file/Assemblaggio_cavo_RJ45_passo_1.jpg)

### Steps 1 and 2

Remove only the jacket, then inspect the inner insulation.

*Figure 3. [Open source and licence.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Assemblaggio_cavo_RJ45_passo_1.jpg)*
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
![Twisted pairs separated for Ethernet termination.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:Redirect/file/Assemblaggio_cavo_RJ45_passo_2.jpg)

### Step 3

Separate the pairs and keep the untwisted length short.

*Figure 4. [Open source and licence.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Assemblaggio_cavo_RJ45_passo_2.jpg)*
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
![Ethernet conductors aligned before entering the modular plug.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:Redirect/file/Assemblaggio_cavo_RJ45_passo_3.jpg)

### Steps 4 to 6

Order, flatten, trim, insert, and check through the clear plug.

*Figure 5. [Open source and licence.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Assemblaggio_cavo_RJ45_passo_3.jpg)*
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
![A photo sequence showing an 8P8C plug being inserted and crimped.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:Redirect/file/Crimping_RJ45_socket_connector.jpg)

### Steps 7 and 8

Crimp fully. Check contact height and strain relief before testing.

*Figure 6. Public-domain visual sequence. [Open source.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Crimping_RJ45_socket_connector.jpg)*
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
![Network cable tester used for modular Ethernet cables.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:Redirect/file/Network_cable_tester_IMGP1639_smial_wp.jpg)

### Step 9

Test for correct order, opens, shorts, reversals, crossed pairs, and split pairs.

*Figure 7. [Open source and licence.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Network_cable_tester_IMGP1639_smial_wp.jpg)*
:::
::::

## Final quality check

- T568B order on both ends.
- No exposed copper or cut insulation.
- Every conductor reaches the front.
- Jacket is under the strain relief.
- All contacts are evenly crimped.
- Tester shows 1 through 8 in order.

## Evidence

Take five photos: stripped jacket, flattened T568B order, head-on view before crimping, finished connector, and tester result.
